card.statement:
A Gelfand--Tsetlin tableau $T(L)$ (equivalently, $L\in{\mathbb C}^{\frac{n(n+1)}{2}}$) is called generic if
$l_{ki}-l_{kj}\notin\mathbb{Z}$ for all $1\leq i\neq j \leq k \leq n-1$.
A character $\chi$ and $\mathsf n = \Ker \chi$ are called generic if $\ell_{\mathsf n}$ is generic for one choice
(hence for all choices) of $\ell_{\mathsf n}$ lying over $\mathsf n$.
A Gelfand--Tsetlin module $M$ will be called a generic Gelfand--Tsetlin module if every $\mathsf n$ in
$\Supp_{\rm GT}(M)$ is generic.
card.label: Definition 6

paper.title: Irreducible Generic Gelfand-Tsetlin Modules of $\mathfrak{gl}(n)$
paper.abstract: We provide a classification and explicit bases of tableaux of all irreducible generic Gelfand-Tsetlin modules for the Lie algebra $\mathfrak{gl}(n)$.
